sights.n: Old Upper Thomson Road (Thomson Road Grand Prix Circuit)
sights.address: Old Upper Thomson Road (through/around Thomson Nature Park), Singapore
sights.w: The surviving loop of the former Thomson Road Grand Prix circuit that hosted the Singapore Grand Prix from 1961 to 1973 — a ~4.8 km course legendary for its danger, with corners nicknamed Devil's Bend, The Snakes and Murder Mile. Now a quiet cycling and walking road on the AMK/Thomson fringe, part of it threading through Thomson Nature Park alongside the old Hainan-village ruins.

sights.address: Teachers' Estate (off Jalan Kuras / Upper Thomson, Yio Chu Kang side), Singapore
sights.w: A landed estate developed by the Singapore Teachers' Union — completed 1969 and officially opened in 1971 by then-Education Minister Lim Kim San — whose roads are named after literary figures such as Tu Fu, Rabindranath Tagore and Munshi Abdullah. A Scenic Fringes marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail.

sights.address: Sembawang Hills Estate (Jalan Leban / Upper Thomson Road vicinity), Singapore
sights.w: A private landed estate on the AMK/Upper Thomson fringe, jointly developed in the 1950s by Bukit Sembawang Rubber Estates and Singapore United Rubber Estates as rubber companies pivoted from a declining plantation trade into housing — one of the earliest such estates. A Scenic Fringes marker on the Ang Mo Kio Heritage Trail, and home to the well-loved Sembawang Hills Food Centre.
